content.text:
That confirms it cleanly — `transactions get pOPE6BjwMa` (a real objectId we saw on the dashboard) returns "Object not found," which is Parse's standard way of masking an ACL denial from a genuine missing record. And the `qbo_sync_events` full record matches the `QboSyncEventAttributes` type exactly (archived, clubObject, dateString, end_date/start_date, number_of_journal_entries, number_of_transactions, status, succeeded_at).

## Spot-check results

Using the "Clubspot (Bot User)" credential from 1Password (signed in via `op run`, so I never saw the actual password):

| Class | Result |
|---|---|
| `qbo_sync_events` | ✅ readable, matches typed shape exactly |
| `chartOfAccounts` | ✅ readable |
| `event_tags` | ✅ readable |
| `ses_email_suppression` | ✅ readable |
| `contracts` | ✅ readable |
| `regattas` | ✅ readable |
| `contact_lists` | ✅ readable |
| `transactions` | ❌ empty / "Object not found" on a known real id |
| `payouts` | ❌ empty |

**The real finding**: `transactions` and `payouts` are ACL-restricted to the `club_admin`/`club_finance` Clubspot roles, and this bot user only carries the `camps` permission — so it can't currently read the general ledger or bank payouts. Everything else across Events/Communication/E-signatures/most of Accounting is readable as-is.

This matters for the treasurer-reconciliation use case specifically: to actually pull `transactions`/`payouts` data, either this bot user needs `club_finance` (or `club_admin`) added in Clubspot's Staff permissions, or a separate credential with that role is needed. I'll add this to the memory note and mention it on the PR — want me to do that now?

1	---
2	name: clubspot-api-discovery-issue-90
3	description: "Parse classes/cloud functions discovered via dashboard network capture for clubspot-sdk expansion (issue #90) — Events, Communication, E-signatures, Accounting/Reporting"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: af521890-4b04-4cb1-8cfb-f169d7b5fa91
8	  modified: 2026-09-09T04:19:03.337Z
9	---
10	
11	Reverse-engineered the Clubspot admin dashboard (theclubspot.com, club id `nw6IMf9Bnq`) via chrome-devtools-mcp network capture to find the Parse classes and `Cloud.run` functions backing four areas not yet in `packages/clubspot-sdk/src/types.ts`. Tracked as GitHub issue [[isthmia-cleanup-initiative|#90]] (not yet implemented as of 2026-09-08 — this is discovery only).
12	
13	**Why:** clubspot-sdk only covered camps/registrations/billing. The user wants read-only SDK coverage of Events, Communication, E-signatures, and Accounting/Reporting to feed a future Clubspot→database sync (Google Groups, WhatsApp, website automation, and per issue #70/#69 the Directus people hub).
14	
15	**How to apply:** When implementing #90 (types.ts/queries.ts/functions.ts additions), start from this list instead of re-exploring the dashboard. Validate against live data with the existing `main.ts` CLI before finalizing shapes — response shapes below are from live CSC production data on 2026-09-08 and may have drifted.
16	
17	## Events
18	- New Parse classes: `events` (social events), `regattas`, `event_tags`, `event_subtypes`.
19	- `registrations` (already modeled) is shared across camps/regattas/events via `eventObject`/`regattaObject` pointers, not just `campObject` — SDK's `RegistrationAttributes` needs those added.
20	- Calendar view uses 5 read-only cloud functions, each `{club_id, start_timestamp, end_timestamp, is_admin}` → lightweight `{id, title, ts, end_ts, type, filter_id}[]`: `retrieve_camps_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_regattas_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_social_events_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_banquets_for_calendar_v2`, `retrieve_group_classes_for_calendar_v2`.
21	
22	## Communication
23	- New classes: `contact_lists`, `member_tags`, `forms`, `email_templates`.
24	- `ses_email_suppression` (bounces/unsubscribes, includes nested `emailObject`/`ses_email_events`) — check before syncing anyone into Google Groups or a newsletter tool.
25	- `ses_campaigns`, `ses_emails` referenced but only reachable via cloud functions, not direct REST queries: `retrieve_sent_campaigns` (`{club_id, search, skip, limit, status, transactional}` → campaign list incl. full recipient `mdb_search` array — PII, handle carefully) and `retrieve_message_stats` (`{club_id, ses_campaign_ids[]}` → open/bounce/recipient counts per campaign).
26	- `check_user_can_remove_from_suppression_list` cloud function also seen (read-only check).
27	
28	## E-signatures
29	- New classes: `contracts` (esignatures.com-backed; `status` fully_signed/signatures_required, `signers`/`signedByArray` with per-signer sign events and timestamps, linked via `campObject`/`regattaObject`/`membershipObject`/`applicationObject`/`registrationObject`/`waiverObject`) and `waivers` (templates, linked to specific camps/events/regattas via an `events` pointer array).
30	- No new cloud functions — standard REST queries only.
31	
32	## Accounting / Reporting
33	Most relevant for treasurer/bookkeeping use cases:
34	- `chartOfAccounts` — full GL account list (code, name, accountType, specialType, QBO mapping in `qbAccountObject`).
35	- `transactions` — **the actual double-entry journal** (this is what "Journal entries" in the nav shows, URL `/accounting/accounting-transactions`). Each row has `lines[]` (debit_acct/credit_acct/amount), `journalsArray` (human-readable account names), `type` (e.g. `order_paid_immediately`, `processing_fees_applied`, `refund_issued`, `invoice_finalized`, `stripe_payout`), linked `orderObject`/`chargeObject`. This is the ground truth ledger — matches QuickBooks after sync.
36	- `qbo_sync_events` — daily QuickBooks Online sync status log: `{start_date, end_date, status, number_of_journal_entries, number_of_transactions, succeeded_at}`. CSC auto-syncs daily at ~3am. Exactly what's needed to build a "did last night's QBO sync succeed" check.
37	- `payouts` — Stripe payout records (amount, arrival date, status, bank destination last-4).
38	- `lineItems` — transaction-line-level detail (heavily nested: orderObject → registrationObject/customer/paymentIntentObject/stripeAccount). More granular than `transactions`, ties revenue lines to specific registrations/participants.
39	- `invoices_membership` — membership billing invoices (separate from camp/event registration billing).
40	- `vendors` — vendor list for manually-entered expenses.
41	- `merch`, `product_subtypes`, `data_views` (saved report configs), `accounting_classes` (QBO "Classes" mapping, empty for CSC).
42	- Cloud functions: `get_line_items_for_channel_summary` (revenue-by-channel time series with comparison period), `getExpensesRunningTotal`, `getTaxSummaryDetails`.

## Summary

Expands `clubspot-sdk` with typed, **read-only** coverage for four areas of the Clubspot dashboard reverse-engineered via live network capture (see #90):

- **Events**: `SocialEvent`, `Regatta`, `EventTag`, `EventSubtype`; `Registration` now models `eventObject`/`regattaObject` alongside the existing `campObject` (now optional, since a registration belongs to exactly one). Adds 5 read-only calendar-feed cloud functions.
- **Communication**: `ContactList`, `MemberTag`, `Form`, `EmailTemplate`, `SesCampaign`, `SesEmail`, `SesEmailEvent`, `SesEmailSuppression` (the bounce/unsubscribe list). Adds `retrieveSentCampaigns` and `retrieveMessageStats` cloud function wrappers.
- **E-signatures**: `Contract` (esignatures.com-backed signing records) and `Waiver` (templates).
- **Accounting/Reporting**: `ChartOfAccounts`, `Transaction` (the actual general-ledger journal - what the dashboard calls "Journal entries"), `QboSyncEvent` (the nightly QuickBooks Online sync status log), `Payout`, `LineItem`, `Order`, `Vendor`, `AccountingClass`, `InvoiceMembership`, `Merch`. Adds `getLineItemsForChannelSummary` and `getExpensesRunningTotal` cloud function wrappers.

Also fleshes out several existing types (`Camp`, `Customer`, `Participant`, `Registration`, `CampClass`) with fields and pointer relationships that were previously left as `-->` TODO comments, now that the target classes (`Merch`, `Waiver`, etc.) exist. A handful of new bare stub classes (`StripeAccount`, `Profile`, `EntryFee`, `RegistrationHold`, `Charge`, `PaymentIntent`, `CustomField`) follow the existing `Shift`/`Courses` pattern for pointer targets whose own attributes haven't been reverse engineered yet.

`queries.ts` gains 6 new query builders mirroring specific dashboard views (cross-event signups, contracts, suppression list, the GL journal, QBO sync history, payouts).

**Strictly read-only** — no `.save()`/`.destroy()` added anywhere. This is intended as the data source for a future Clubspot → database sync (see #69/#70), and separately gives useful read access for treasurer/bookkeeping reconciliation (comparing Clubspot's ledger against what actually landed in QuickBooks/the bank).

Where field shapes weren't confirmed against live data, they're left as explicit `TODO` comments rather than guessed.

Done. Summary of what happened:

**Spot-checks confirmed the SDK is solid** — `qbo_sync_events`, `chartOfAccounts`, `event_tags`, `ses_email_suppression`, `contracts`, `regattas`, and `contact_lists` all read cleanly against live data with the bot credential, and `qbo_sync_events` matched the typed shape exactly.

**Real permissions finding**: the existing Clubspot API bot user is scoped to the `camps` permission only, so it can't read `transactions` (the GL ledger) or `payouts` — those need `club_finance`/`club_admin`, which your own account has. This matters directly for your treasurer-reconciliation idea: whoever runs that sync will need the bot user upgraded, or a separate privileged credential.

**Testing with your account also caught two type gaps**, now fixed and pushed:
- `Transaction` gets `sync_status`/`sync_event_id`/`qbo_journal_id`/`qbo_synced_at` once a row has actually synced to QBO (my earlier capture happened to be from a not-yet-synced row).
- `Payout` was missing `balanceTransactionID`, `destinationID`, `fingerprint`, `netAmount`, `brand`.

Both credentials were used via `op run` (1Password CLI), so I never saw either plaintext password — only resolved session/whoami output and query results.

PR #91 is updated: build/lint/test still clean, checklist item checked off, and a new "Spot-check results" section documents the permissions finding. Memory is updated too, so this doesn't need re-discovering later. Let me know if you want the bot user's Clubspot role actually changed — that's a config change in Clubspot itself, not something I'd do without you saying so explicitly.
